Q1.A. Refer above table and find the joint probability of the people who planned to purchase and actually placed an order. [1 Mark]¶

#People who planned and actually placed order PY
PY = 400
#Total People
TP = 2000
#joint probability of the people who planned to purchase and actually placed an order
P = 400/2000
print("joint probability of the people who planned to purchase and actually placed an order:",P)

joint probability of the people who planned to purchase and actually placed an order: 0.2
1.B. Refer to the above table and find the joint probability of the people who planned to purchase and actually placed an order, given that people planned to purchase. [1 Mark]¶
In [10]:
#People who planned to purchase and actualy placed an order
PY = 400
#Total Planned to Purchase
TPP = 500
#Total People
TP = 2000
#joint probability of the people who planned to purchase and actually placed an order, given that people planned to purchase
P = (400/2000)/(500/2000)
print("joint probability of the people who planned to purchase and actually placed an order, given that people planned to purchase:",P)

joint probability of the people who planned to purchase and actually placed an order, given that people planned to purchase: 0.8
2. An electrical manufacturing company conducts quality checks at specified periods on the products it manufactures. Historically, the failure rate for the manufactured item is 5%. Suppose a random sample of 10 manufactured items is selected. Answer the following questions. [4 Marks]¶
In [18]:
import numpy as np
import scipy.stats as stats
n=10 #Sample size
p=0.05 #Failure rate of the manufactured item
k=np.arange(0,11) #Array of quantiles
binomial = stats.binom.pmf(k,n,p)
binomial

3. A car salesman sells on an average 3 cars per week.¶
In [40]:
rate = 3
n=np.arange(0,17)
3.A. What is Probability that in a given week he will sell some cars? [1 Mark]¶
In [41]:
#cumulative poisson distribution
poisson_c = stats.poisson.cdf(n,rate)
#Probability that in a given week he will sell some cars
p=1-poisson_c[0]
print("Probability that in a given week he will sell some cars: ",p)

Probability that in a given week he will sell some cars:  0.950212931632136
3.B. What is Probability that in a given week he will sell 2 or more but less than 5 cars? [1 Mark]¶
In [44]:
#Probability that he sells less than 5 cars i.e upto 4 cars
P1 = poisson_c[4]
#Probability that he sells less than 2 cars i.e up to 1 car
P2 = poisson_c[1]
#Probability that in a given week he will sell 2 or more but less than 5 cars
P=P1-P2
print("Probability that in a given week he will sell 2 or more but less than 5 cars: ",P)

Probability that in a given week he will sell 2 or more but less than 5 cars:  0.6161149710523164
3.C. Plot the poisson distribution function for cumulative probability of cars sold per-week vs number of cars sold per week. [1 Mark]¶

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
%matplotlib inline

plt.plot(n,poisson_c, 'o-')
plt.title('Poisson Distribution')
plt.xlabel('Number of cars sold per week')
plt.ylabel('Cumulative Probability of cars sold per week')
plt.show()

5. Explain 1 real life industry scenario (other than the ones mentioned above) where you can use the concepts learnt in this module of Applied Statistics to get data driven business solution. [3 Marks]¶

Problem Statement¶

A company ABC every year provides AWS Solution Architect certification training to its 50 employees on first come first serve basis and gives the vouchure to appear in the exam at free of cost. The company has been doing this from last 7 years. The success rate to pass the certification exam is 60%.

Answer the following question?¶

Find the probility that none of the employee passes the exam?
Find the probability that exactly 20 employees pass the exam?
Find the probability that 25 or more passes the exam?

The above real life problem statement is based on Probability Distribution and Binomial Distribution

In [94]:
n=50 #sample size
p=0.6 #probability to pass the certification exam based on historic data as given
k=np.arange(0,51) #array of quantiles
binomial=stats.binom.pmf(k,n,p) #probability mass function

#Find the probility that none of the employee passes the exam
print("Probility that none of the employee passes the exam: %.5f" %binomial[0])

#Find the probability that exactly 20 employees pass the exam
print("Probability that exactly 20 employees pass the exam: %.5f" %binomial[20])

#Find the probability that 25 or more passes the exam
binomial_c=stats.binom.cdf(k,n,p) #cumulative density function
print("Probability that 25 or more passes the exam: %.5f" %(1-binomial_c[24]))

# Let us plot the distribution for number of successes and its probability
plt.bar(k, binomial)
plt.title("Binomial Distribution: n=%i , p=%.2f" % (n, p))
plt.xlabel("Number of Successes") 
plt.ylabel("Probability of Successes")
plt.show() 

Probility that none of the employee passes the exam: 0.00000
Probability that exactly 20 employees pass the exam: 0.00199
Probability that 25 or more passes the exam: 0.94266

Part B¶

DOMAIN: Sports¶

• CONTEXT: Company X manages the men's top professional basketball division of the American league system. The dataset contains information on all the teams that have participated in all the past tournaments. It has data about how many baskets each team scored, conceded, how many times they came within the first 2 positions, how many tournaments they have qualified, their best position in the past, etc.
• DATA DESCRIPTION: Basketball.csv - The data set contains information on all the teams so far participated in all the past tournaments.
• DATA DICTIONARY:

  1. Team: Team’s name
  2. Tournament: Number of played tournaments.
  3. Score: Team’s score so far.
  4. PlayedGames: Games played by the team so far.
  5. WonGames: Games won by the team so far.
  6. DrawnGames: Games drawn by the team so far.
  7. LostGames: Games lost by the team so far.
  8. BasketScored: Basket scored by the team so far.
  9. BasketGiven: Basket scored against the team so far.
  10. TournamentChampion: How many times the team was a champion of the tournaments so far.
  11. Runner-up: How many times the team was a runners-up of the tournaments so far.
  12. TeamLaunch: Year the team was launched on professional basketball.

  13. HighestPositionHeld: Highest position held by the team amongst all the tournaments played.
    • PROJECT OBJECTIVE: Company’s management wants to invest on proposals on managing some of the best teams in the league. The analytics department has been assigned with a task of creating a report on the performance shown by the teams. Some of the older teams are already in contract with competitors. Hence Company X wants to understand which teams they can approach which will be a deal win for them.

    ##### STEPS AND TASK [30 Marks]:

  • TeamLaunch column has years in different formats: E.g
  • 1929
  • 1941-42 separated by Hyphen -
  • 1999to00 separated by to
  • 201617 separated by underscore
  • 1951~52 separated by tild ~
  • 0 to 1 year difference in start and end year

Replace to, _ , ~ to - to make it similar to other values¶

In [319]:
df_new['TeamLaunch'] = df_new['TeamLaunch'].replace(["to",'_','~'],'-',regex=True)
In [334]:
#Adding a new column TeamLaunchStartYear
df_new['TeamLaunchStartYear'] = df_new['TeamLaunch'].str.split('-').str[0]
df_new['TeamLaunchStartYear'] = df_new['TeamLaunchStartYear'].astype('int64')
  • we have converted the new column TeamLaunchStartYear as integer as we have just year and not the day,time,date,month etc. Hence taking it as integer would also work in case if we require any comparison with the year
  • We will be introducing new column TeamLaunchEndYear of int64 type
  • TeamLaunchEndYear is always going to be TeamLaunchStartYear + 1 except for year 1929 based on the current data observation from file
In [339]:
#populate TeamLaunchEndYear values as per below condition
df_new['TeamLaunchEndYear'] = np.where(df_new['TeamLaunchStartYear']==1929,1929,df_new['TeamLaunchStartYear']+1)
In [340]:
#we can drop TeamLaunch column as it looks like data in this format might not be needed for any comparision etc. 
#and also we have derived TeamLaunchStartYear and TeamLaunchEndYear columns from this and converted in in useful data.
df_new.drop('TeamLaunch',axis=1,inplace=True)

3. Please include any improvements or suggestions to the association management on quality, quantity, variety, velocity, veracity etc. on the data points collected by the association to perform a better data analysis in future. At-least 1 suggestion for each point. [10 Marks]¶

Yes, There would be various suggestion on improvement of data on below various factors:

Quality of data:¶

  • TeamLaunch column: which indicates year the team was launch was not consistent throughout, the year was of various format like 1929, 1930-31, 1932_32,1931to32,1931~32 the separator was not common between start & end year. This type of data can make sense only for manual analysis by human. We needed to convert this data in meaningful format. like we made a consistent approach to separate it by only hypen and replaced all underscore,to,tild etc to hyphen and then also derived 2 columns out of this as teamLaunchStartYear and TeamLaunchEndYear so that we can so any analysis based on year. So the data coluld have collected using a dropdown and not through a open textbox where user can write the way he/she can write in his/her desired format. So we should have collected this column data in a proper format
  • Team61 has most of the columns as null which makes no sense, hence we deleted that row from our analysis.
  • TournamentChampions and Runner-up was having many columns as null we should have given 0 if the team did not become champion or Runner-up ever. we needed to convert them to 0 in place of null for these columns based on assumptions.

Quantity:¶

  • Quantity of data was very less,it was just 61 rows. Looked like it was summarised data already about team. the total score, wongames, playedgames etc was summarised per team. i.e Team level information was there but tournament level information was not there which could have helped analyse from tournament level perspective as well.

Variety:¶

  • Variety of data was less, we did not had Player level information to get more insight into player performance.

Velocity:¶

  • Data was till 2016 only and that too was not continuous for every year. Latest and complete data could have given better insights.
  • Data collection could have automated then the chance of errors for TeamLaunch column could have reduced.
  • Few fields could have been made manadatory, so that 0 could have been entered instead of null for integer fields if and only if the data can not be null.

Veracity:¶

  • We could have applied data validation while collecting data so that it can come it appropriate format and the chances of errors in data could have got minimized. Ex. TeamLaunch
  • Integer fields should have got defaulted to zero value
  • HighestPositionHeld, which means Highest position held by the team amongst all the tournaments played, has lack of clearance on what it means if we looks at data, Those who played highest number tournament has less times highestpositionheld and those who played just 1 tournament have 20 times holded highest position, hopefully it should be based on number of PlayedGames in the tournament.

Part C¶

DOMAIN: Startup ecosystem¶

CONTEXT: Company X is a EU online publisher focusing on the startups industry. The company specifically reports on the business related to technology news, analysis of emerging trends and profiling of new tech businesses and products. Their event i.e. Startup Battlefield is the world’s pre-eminent startup competition. Startup Battlefield features 15-30 top early stage startups pitching top judges in front of a vast live audience, present in person and online.
DATA DESCRIPTION: CompanyX_EU.csv - Each row in the dataset is a Start-up company and the columns describe the company.
DATA DICTIONARY:
1. Startup: Name of the company
2. Product: Actual product
3. Funding: Funds raised by the company in USD
4. Event: The event the company participated in
5. Result: Described by Contestant, Finalist, Audience choice, Winner or Runner up
6. OperatingState: Current status of the company, Operating ,Closed, Acquired or IPO
Dataset has been downloaded from the internet. All the credit for the dataset goes to the original creator of the data.
PROJECT OBJECTIVE: Analyse the data of the various companies from the given dataset and perform the tasks that are specified in the below
steps. Draw insights from the various attributes that are present in the dataset, plot distributions, state hypotheses and draw conclusions from the dataset.
STEPS AND TASK [15 Marks]:

4. Statistical Analysis: [10 Marks]¶
A. Is there any significant difference between Funds raised by companies that are still operating vs companies that closed down? [1 Mark]¶

We will do hypothesis testing to get answer of this question, let us visualize this a bit for better understanding¶

In [639]:
startup_filter = startup.loc[(startup['OperatingState'].isin(['Operating','Closed']))]
plt.figure(figsize=(15,5))
sns.boxplot(data=startup_filter,x='OperatingState',y='Funds_in_million')
plt.show()
  • It is not very clear to identify difference here due to a lot of outliers for operating
  • we will zoom in a bit to compare the closed and operating one
In [640]:
plt.figure(figsize=(15,5))
sns.boxplot(data=startup_filter,x='OperatingState',y='Funds_in_million')
plt.ylim(0,250)
plt.show()
  • All the startup which were closed were less funded compared to operating ones but yes it is also important to mention that few startups have similar Funding as closed ones, but they are still operating

Let us to Hypothesis testing to identify the answer of this question¶

  • 2 independent samples are given
    • first thoses startups which are closed
    • second those startups which are operating

Hence it would be a 2 sample independent ttest¶

  • H0: "There is no significant difference between Funds raised by companies that are still operating vs companies that closed down"
  • HA: "There is significant difference between Funds raised by companies that are still operating vs companies that closed down"
In [672]:
import scipy.stats as stats
#Operating Startup Funds_in_million sample
OStartupFundsInMillion = startup.loc[startup['OperatingState']=='Operating']['Funds_in_million']
#Closed Startup Funds_in_million sample
CStartupFundsInMillion = startup.loc[startup['OperatingState']=='Closed']['Funds_in_million']
#Consider level of significance as 0.05
alpha=0.05
#Do 2 sample independent ttest
t_statistic, p_value = stats.ttest_ind(OStartupFundsInMillion, CStartupFundsInMillion, equal_var=True)
print('t_statistic:', t_statistic, "\np_value:",p_value)

if(p_value<alpha):
    print("There is significant difference between Funds raised by companies that are still operating vs companies that closed down")
else:
    print("There is no significant difference between Funds raised by companies that are still operating vs companies that closed down")
    

t_statistic: 1.1382924515740138 
p_value: 0.25572701885629406
There is no significant difference between Funds raised by companies that are still operating vs companies that closed down
B. Write the null hypothesis and alternative hypothesis. [1 Mark]¶

Null Hypothesis:¶

H0: "There is no significant difference between Funds raised by companies that are still operating vs companies that closed down"

Alternate Hypothesis:¶

HA: "There is significant difference between Funds raised by companies that are still operating vs companies that closed down"

C. Test for significance and conclusion [1 Mark]¶
In [674]:
import scipy.stats as stats
#Operating Startup Funds_in_million sample
OStartupFundsInMillion = startup.loc[startup['OperatingState']=='Operating']['Funds_in_million']
#Closed Startup Funds_in_million sample
CStartupFundsInMillion = startup.loc[startup['OperatingState']=='Closed']['Funds_in_million']
#Consider level of significance as 0.05
alpha=0.05
#Do 2 sample independent ttest
t_statistic, p_value = stats.ttest_ind(OStartupFundsInMillion, CStartupFundsInMillion, equal_var=True)
print('t_statistic:', t_statistic, "\np_value:",p_value)

if(p_value<alpha):
    print("There is significant difference between Funds raised by companies that are still operating vs companies that closed down")
else:
    print("There is no significant difference between Funds raised by companies that are still operating vs companies that closed down")
    

t_statistic: 1.1382924515740138 
p_value: 0.25572701885629406
There is no significant difference between Funds raised by companies that are still operating vs companies that closed down

Conclusion:¶

  • Since p_value is greater than alpha i.e level of significance, we fail to reject the null hypothesis which means There is no significant difference between funds raised by companies that are still operating vs companies that closed down.

G. Write your hypothesis comparing the proportion of companies that are operating between winners and contestants: [2 Mark]¶

Null Hypothesis:
H0: Proportion of operating companies is the same for both winners and contestants
Alternate Hypothesis:
HA: Proportion of operating companies is not the same for both winners and contestants

In [795]:
#consider level of significance alpha as 0.05
alpha = 0.05
#Chisquare test
test_stat, pval, dof, expected_value = stats.chi2_contingency(observed = startupdf.values)
pval
Out[795]:
1.0
H. Test for significance and conclusion [1 Mark]¶
In [796]:
#Test for significance
if pval<alpha :
    print("We reject the null hpothesis i.e Proportion of operating companies is not the same for both winners and contestants")
else: 
    print("We failed to reject the null hpothesis meaning Proportion of operating companies is the same for both winners and contestants")
    

We failed to reject the null hpothesis meaning Proportion of operating companies is the same for both winners and contestants

Conclusion:

  • Since pval is greater than level of significance, We failed to reject the null hypothesis that means Yes the Proportion of operating companies is the same for both winners and contestants
